learningObjective: Diagnose per-metric bottlenecks (TTFT vs TPOT) from serving-side data.

canonicalClaims.claim: P99 TTFT tail under load with nontrivial preemption rate is a signature of KV cache pressure causing queueing and preempt-and-resume overhead; direct levers are KV footprint reduction (MQA/GQA, quant, shorter context).
conditions: Serving uses continuous batching with preemption.
Prompt lengths large relative to KV budget per sequence.
nonImplications: Does not imply KV quant is accuracy-neutral.
Does not imply all TTFT tail is preemption-caused.

canonicalClaims.claim: Decode utilization ~25% at batch-1 or small batch is consistent with memory-bandwidth-bound decode; TPOT is set by KV/weight bandwidth, not compute.
nonImplications: Does not imply utilization is a bug; it is normal for bandwidth-bound kernels.

misconceptions.claim: High compute utilization indicates memory-bound behavior.
misconceptions.whyWrong: High SM utilization means SMs are busy; that is compute-bound.

misconceptions.claim: Increasing batch size always improves throughput without hurting TPOT.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Larger batch increases per-step compute time and thus TPOT; there is a latency-throughput trade-off.

misconceptions.claim: Preemption never affects TTFT for the preempted request.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Preemption pushes TTFT (for that request's first-token) further out by whatever the resume cost is.

implementationFacts: Preemption rate is often reported by serving frameworks as a first-class metric.
SGLang/vLLM expose queue-depth and effective batch size histograms for diagnosis.
performanceScenarios: Long-context serving is the most common driver of KV-pressure-driven TTFT tail.
